title: Reading a monster before it reaches you
summary: R.E.P.O.'s monsters are not one behaviour with different skins: the game tracks a state and a type for them, and each kind is built around a different way of hurting your crew.
body: The game tracks what a monster is currently doing, which means a monster moving calmly is a different situation from one already committed to an attack.
Monsters are also typed, so a crew can learn to recognise a kind rather than reacting to every noise the same way.
The differences are physical rather than cosmetic: one kind spins, another throws something at you, and the shapes you see tell you which response is worth trying.
What this entry does not tell you: how long any state lasts, the reach of an attack or how much it hurts. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Every monster carries a tracked behaviour state.
Monsters are typed, so kinds can be told apart.
At least one monster is built around spinning.
At least one monster throws something at the crew.

alt.en: Diagram: you hear a monster, you identify the kind, you pick a response, and the crew keeps moving.
